capabilities.description: Features this daemon has: a list of names, one per feature added after harness.v1 first shipped; a client checks for the name before offering the feature, and ignores names it doesn't know. `run.controls`: POST /v1/runs/{runId}/pause, /resume and /cancel; `agents.messages`: POST /v1/runs/{runId}/agents/{agentId}/messages: steer an agent with a message; `steer.skills`: POST …/agents/{agentId}/messages takes `skills`: names from GET /v1/skills, sent to the agent with the message; `agent.pause`: POST /v1/runs/{runId}/agents/{agentId}/pause and /resume: one agent and its descendants; `runs.options`: POST /v1/runs takes `driver` (claude or codex), `effort` (the driver's reasoning effort) and `sandbox` (docker or boxd); GET /v1/run-options lists them and whether each is available; `runs.options.repo`: GET /v1/run-options takes `repo` (a project checkout, as POST /v1/runs `repo`): the options for a run of that project, with its own agent profiles; `runs.options.sandbox`: GET /v1/run-options `drivers[].sandboxes`: whether each driver can run in each sandbox (logins and agent environments are per sandbox); POST /v1/runs refuses a `driver` and `sandbox` that can't go together (422); `runs.options.models`: GET /v1/run-options `drivers[].models`: the models each driver's planner can run on (an id, a display name and a one-line note); POST /v1/runs takes `model`, one of them; `agent.steps`: agent.step events: one durable event per finished step of an agent (its kind, count, start and end), in order, replayed by GET /v1/events and delivered on run streams; `logins`: GET /v1/logins: whether agents can log in to Claude and Codex in each sandbox, how (plan or API key), and the command that logs in; `environments`: GET /v1/environments: each sandbox's agent environment (ready, missing, building or failed), its tool versions, and the command that builds it; `service`: GET /v1/service: whether capcomd runs as a background service (installed, loaded), and the commands that install and uninstall it; `sandboxes`: GET /v1/sandboxes and /v1/sandboxes/{name}: each place agents run as a provider descriptor (label, kind, caps, which settings, info rows and actions it has), with its settings and info as typed fields; GET /v1/logins and /v1/environments take `sandbox`, and logins carry `hostBound` and `boundTo`; `sandboxes.resources`: GET /v1/sandboxes/{name}/resources and …/resources/{id}: the machines capcomd's agents run on at that place (owned by an agent, or orphaned), and the `capcomd sandbox shell` command that opens a shell in one; `sandboxes.settings`: PATCH /v1/sandboxes/{name}/settings (the `configure` scope): change a place's settings (the idle machine lifetime; Docker's memory per agent); fields carry `editable` and `source`, and each change is a sandbox.settings_changed event on the daemon stream. Machines of capcomd's own jobs (checks, logins, environment builds) carry an owner of their `kind` instead of reading as orphaned; `sandboxes.actions`: POST /v1/sandboxes/{name}/resources/{id}/actions/delete (the steer scope, an Idempotency-Key): delete a machine. An agent's machine is deleted by cancelling that agent, a machine left behind by its provider; capcomd's own jobs' machines can't be. Resources carry `destructive` and the daemon's `confirm` question; sandbox.resource_action and sandbox.resource_deleted audit it on the daemon stream; `projects.setup`: GET /v1/projects/inspect and POST /v1/projects (the `configure` scope, an Idempotency-Key): set up a folder on the daemon's machine as a capcomd project (a GitHub checkout), as `capcomd setup project` does, and add it to capcomd's projects; each setup is a project.configured event on the daemon stream; `projects.known`: GET /v1/projects/known: capcomd's projects with their checkout folders on the daemon's machine, and which is the default; `projects.git`: POST /v1/projects/git-init, GET /v1/projects/publish-options and POST /v1/projects/publish (the `configure` scope for the POSTs, each with an Idempotency-Key): take a plain folder to a GitHub checkout before setting it up: start a git repository in it, then create its GitHub repository with the GitHub CLI (the first commit made when there is none, likely secrets refused) and push. Audited as project.git_initialized and project.published on the daemon stream. POST /v1/projects takes `check` as optional and `gitignore`; `runs.goal_branch`: Goal branches: POST /v1/runs takes `base` and `goalBranch`; Run.goalBranch; GET /v1/projects/branches (the base menu and the suggested goal branch); GET /v1/runs/{runId}/goal (the branch against its base, what landed and what didn't, the planner's summary); POST /v1/runs/{runId}/pull-request and /keep-branch (the steer scope); run.goal_completed, run.pr_opened and run.branch_kept events; `agents.title`: Agent titles: Agent.title and titleSource (the user's, else the agent's own, its parent's or the driving harness's, else derived from the task); PUT and DELETE /v1/runs/{runId}/agents/{agentId}/title (the steer scope): the user's title, which sticks until they clear it; agent.titled on run streams and the lifecycle feed; Run.titleSource agent (the planner named the run) and run.titled; `agents.thread_tail`: GET /v1/runs/{runId}/agents/{agentId}/thread/tail: an agent's newest thread items by position, with `before` (the page above them, for scrolling up) and `cursor` (where GET …/thread and live frames take over), so a long thread opens on its latest messages; `plugins`: GET /v1/plugins: every plugin the daemon discovered, in load order, with its lifecycle state, why it failed or is disabled, the hooks and seams it contributes and its hook call statistics; GET /v1/plugins/{name} (its manifest and config, never a secret); POST /v1/plugins/{name}/enable and /disable (the configure scope, an Idempotency-Key); plugin.* events on the daemon stream audit the plugin host; `profiles`: GET /v1/profiles: every agent profile a run can use (the daemon's, or with `repo` a project's): its version, the layer it was found in and the files laid together to make it, what it does, its provider, model and tool mode, and whether its login is there; `plugins.protocol`: The out-of-process plugin protocol, version 1 (spec §9): a plugin capcomd starts opens POST /v1/plugins/{name}/sessions, reads its hook calls on GET /v1/plugins/{name}/hooks (SSE), answers with POST /v1/plugins/{name}/hooks/{callId}, writes its events with POST /v1/plugins/{name}/events and keeps data in /v1/plugins/{name}/storage. Only the token the daemon minted for that plugin's process may call them; plugin.process_changed audits its process; `triggers`: Triggers from sources (plugin API §16.3): trigger.received, trigger.subscribed, trigger.unsubscribed and trigger.replied on the daemon stream audit what the intake decided about each external event and what a run answered; Run.trigger names the trigger a run started from; `profiles.edit`: GET /v1/profiles/{name}: one profile as typed rows a client renders and edits (each with the file that sets it, `source` and `editable`) and its `rev`; PUT /v1/profiles/{name} (the `configure` scope, an Idempotency-Key): change them in the profile's own file, its version bumped; each write is a profile.changed event on the daemon stream; `plugins.config`: Plugin install, trust and config layers (plugin API §4.8, §10): POST /v1/runs takes `plugins`, a run's per-run plugin settings; GET /v1/plugins/{name} config `sources` says which layer each value came from (default, user, project, env); a project's plugins (source project) stay validated with cause untrusted until the operator trusts their content; plugin.trusted on the daemon stream audits a trust; `profiles.facts`: GET /v1/profiles rows (and GET /v1/profiles/{name}'s `profile`) carry what a planner chooses by: `title` (untrusted), `fit` (a daemon-written sentence), `cost`, `canReport`, the `skills` its agents are pinned with (names and hashes, never their text) `untrustedSkills`, the project skills a spawn of it waits on the operator's trust for, `untrustedPersona`, its project persona when a spawn of it waits on the same, and `untrustedSandbox`, the project's profile files that set its `sandbox.provider` when a spawn of it on a run without a sandbox of its own waits on the same; `runs.options.planners`: GET /v1/run-options `planners`: every profile that can plan, each with whether a run can start with it now and why not (its login, untrusted project skills, an untrusted project file that sets its sandbox.provider (a run started with a `sandbox` of its own doesn't wait on it), a sandbox.provider outside the run's isolation, a sandbox.environment that isn't built, no agent environment, an egress limit its sandbox can't enforce, a lifecycle plugin that isn't active); `plugins.routes`: Plugin API routes (plugin API §4.7.3): METHOD /v1/x/{plugin}/… serves a plugin's own routes, JSON in and out, with the caller's token, which needs the scope the route declares (403 `forbidden` otherwise; 404 `not_found` for a route no active plugin serves; a plugin's failure is 500 `internal` with the message "plugin error"). GET /v1/plugins/{name} lists its `routes` and the `capabilities` it adds here, named x.<plugin>.<flag>; `context.brain_proposals`: A run's proposals to a company's brain (ADR-025 step 5): GET /v1/runs/{runId}/brain-proposals lists them and whether each was sent; POST /v1/runs/{runId}/brain-proposals/send (the `configure` scope, an Idempotency-Key) sends those waiting for a person as the caller (groundray's actor human:<client id>), as `capcomd context brain propose --run <runId> --yes` does. This daemon always sends it; optional because daemons from before capabilities don't: treat a missing list as empty

post.description: Capability projects.setup. Set a folder up as a capcomd project, as `capcomd setup project` does with the same answers: <checkout>/.capcomd/config.json (repository, merge mode, target, the check, the reviewer; a spend cap when asked), merged into what's there, and a profile file per profile in <checkout>/.capcomd/profiles/ (<name>.yaml: a worker per agent, a read-only reviewer, a lead, the memory consolidator and a planner that may spawn them), keeping profiles that exist; then the folder joins capcomd's projects. Every file is written atomically, and only inside the checkout. The repository is always the checkout's origin (GET /v1/projects/inspect `repo`), never a URL from the client; only GitHub checkouts. Needs the `configure` scope (403 `forbidden` without it), like changing a place's settings. Everything is checked again: 422 `invalid` with the daemon's sentence and `field` (path, mode, target, check, agents, budgetUsd) for a folder inspect reports a problem for (`problem` is its code), pull requests without `ghReady`, a target that isn't a branch name, an unknown or repeated agent, a budget when none is asked (or not over 0), or a .capcomd that leads out of the checkout (a symlink). 409 `conflict` when origin isn't `expect.repo` (the body carries `repo`, the origin now). Audited: a durable project.configured event on the `daemon` stream when something changed. `Idempotency-Key` (8-200 chars, required) is scoped to the calling client and kept 24h: same key + same body: 200 with the first result (replay, nothing written again); same key + another body: 409 `idempotency_conflict`. Only a 200 is kept. Afterwards GET /v1/run-options?repo=<root> answers for the project.

post.description: Capability projects.git. Publish a checkout without origin to GitHub: when it has no commits, `git add -A` (what .gitignore ignores stays out) and a first commit "Initial commit"; then `gh repo create <owner>/<name> --private|--public --source <root> --remote origin --push` on the daemon's machine, which creates the repository, adds it as origin and pushes the current branch. Can take a while (it waits for the push). Needs the `configure` scope (403 `forbidden` without it). Returns the checkout's inspect result as it is now (`github` set: it can be set up with POST /v1/projects). Refusals carry the daemon's sentence and `field`: 422 `invalid` for a folder that isn't a checkout without origin (path, with `problem`), the GitHub CLI not logged in (gh), an owner that isn't in `accounts` or a name GitHub doesn't take (owner, name); without commits: likely secrets among the files (files; the sentence names them and says to add them to .gitignore), more than 2000 files (files: add a .gitignore), no files, or no git user.name/email (identity). 409 `conflict` with `field` name when the repository already exists on GitHub, and without a field when the checkout already has an origin or is being published. 503 `unavailable` when the GitHub CLI fails otherwise (its first line in the sentence). A first commit that was made stays when the GitHub step fails: publishing again pushes it. Audited: a durable project.published event on the `daemon` stream (owner, name, visibility and a file count, never file names or contents). `Idempotency-Key` (8-200 chars, required) as for POST /v1/projects.

Title: the run's goal; description: the planner's summary, then what each agent landed and how it was reviewed, then what didn't. capcomd never merges it. A run whose planner stopped before it finished (state stopped: it failed or was cancelled) is 409 `stopped` with the question to ask the person ("The planner stopped before it finished (it failed): 2 of 3 tasks landed on <branch>. post.description: Capability context.brain_proposals. Send the run's proposals not sent yet to their brains as you (body optional: `{"agentId": "agt-…"}`), as `capcomd context brain propose --run <runId> --yes` does: each becomes a draft on the run's proposal branch of the brain's repository (written by groundray with the actor human:<your client id>) and a pull request there for the brain's owners; what agents read doesn't change. Those sent already stay as they were (`already`), whoever sent them; a proposal the brain already holds (its pull request merged) isn't drafted again. Each one sent is a plugin.context.brain_proposed event on the run stream. 200 once every proposal is sent (`sent` empty: the run proposed nothing). 503 `unavailable` when one or more couldn't be sent (the brain or groundray didn't answer, or refused): the body adds `sent`, each with its `error`; those sent stay sent, so send again (with the same Idempotency-Key or a new one) for the rest. Needs the `configure` scope: the drafts are written in your name in another repository. A plugin's token is 403 `forbidden`: a plugin never sends a proposal in a person's name. `Idempotency-Key` (8-200 chars) is scoped to the calling client and kept 24h: the same key and body answer the first 200 again without sending; the same key with another run or body is 409 `idempotency_conflict`. 404 `not_found` for an unknown run.

post.description: Steer: send the agent a message from the operator (`capcomd send <runId> <agt> <text>`). Returns the thread `seq`; the message.sent event on the run stream with the same `data.seq` (and `data.to` = agentId) confirms it, so a client can match its optimistic bubble. 409 `conflict` when the agent has ended (nothing would read it). 422 `invalid` when `body` is empty or over 1048576 bytes, or a skill is unknown or too many. The same key with other `skills` is another request (409 `idempotency_conflict`). Needs the steer scope. `Idempotency-Key` (8-200 chars) is scoped to the calling client and kept 24h: same key + same request: 200 with the first result (replay); same key on a different request (another route, run, agent or body): 409 `idempotency_conflict`. Errors: 404 `not_found` (unknown run or agent), 409 `conflict` (state), 422 `invalid`.

post.description: Capability agent.pause. Pause one agent and its descendants (no body), as `capcomd pause <runId> <agt>`; the rest of the run keeps working. One that hasn't started is paused now (`changed`); a running one is asked to stop (`pending`): at its next check (about every 2 s) it stops, its work is committed and pushed to its branch (`Capcomd-Stop: paused`), and it is paused. Confirmed by agent.paused per agent (data.result.limit "paused", data.result.by client:<id>). The run's own state follows its agents: run.paused when this leaves every live agent of the run paused, else the run stays running. 409 `conflict` when neither the agent nor any descendant is pending or running. Needs the steer scope. `Idempotency-Key` (8-200 chars) is scoped to the calling client and kept 24h: same key + same request: 200 with the first result (replay); same key on a different request (another route, run, agent or body): 409 `idempotency_conflict`. Errors: 404 `not_found` (unknown run or agent), 409 `conflict` (state), 422 `invalid`.

post.description: Capability sandboxes.actions. Act on one machine; today the only action is delete (no body, no parameters). Needs the steer scope (403 `forbidden` without it), like cancelling a run. An agent's machine: that agent (and the agents it started) is cancelled through the normal cancel path, as POST …/cancel and `capcomd cancel <runId> <agt>` do (agent.cancelled on the run stream), and its lifecycle destroys the machine; the provider is never called for it directly. A machine left behind (`orphaned`): the provider deletes it. A machine of capcomd's own jobs (checks, logins, environment builds): 409 `conflict`. The id must be a machine capcomd lists at this place (only ids with capcomd's prefix, and only machines a live owner holds or this capcomd's machines ledger records: another capcomd's machine is 404 and never reaches the provider; no batch or wildcard ids). Right before acting the daemon reads the machine again: when who uses it changed (an orphan an agent now uses, an agent that ended) it is 409 `conflict` and nothing is deleted; a machine already gone is 200 with `changed: false`. One action at a time per machine (another one under way: 409). 503 `unavailable` when the provider (or capcomd's records) doesn't answer in time: nothing was deleted, or, when the agent was already asked to stop, its machine may still go. 404 `not_found` for a place that isn't listed, an unknown machine, an unknown action, open_terminal (read with GET …/resources/{id}), or an action the place's provider doesn't declare. Audited on the daemon stream: sandbox.resource_action {sandbox, resourceId, action, owner, clientId}, then sandbox.resource_deleted {sandbox, resourceId, cause: action}. `Idempotency-Key` (8-200 chars, required: 422 `invalid` without it) is scoped to the calling client and kept 24h: same key + same request: 200 with the first result (replay, nothing deleted twice); the same key on another machine or action: 409 `idempotency_conflict`. Only a 200 is kept: after an error, a retry looks again.

get.description: Capability plugins.protocol. Only the token the daemon minted for this plugin's running process (CAPCOMD_PLUGIN_TOKEN), whatever its scopes: 403 `forbidden` for any other; 409 `conflict` when the plugin has no process running. The session's hook calls (spec §9.4), SSE: `event:` is the frame (hook.call, hook.dropped, session.closing), `id:` its seq, heartbeat comments every 15 s. One stream per session (a second closes the first with session.closing reason replaced). Last-Event-ID resumes: the frames after it again, and the open gate call (same callId); a gap past the 1 000 kept is a hook.dropped. Gate and modify calls come one at a time (the next after this one is answered or its deadline passes); observe calls as they happen, queued while no stream is open (1 000 frames or 4 MB, then the oldest are dropped and counted). Closed for 60 s, the plugin is disconnected: its gate calls fail (denied). 409 `conflict` for a session that isn't this start's, or isn't open.

Needs the `read` scope. Local files only. Never contains a credential or a prompt's text. `repo` as GET /v1/profiles (422 `invalid` when it isn't a project checkout). 404 `not_found` for a name that isn't a profile; 422 `invalid` when the profiles can't be read (`message` says why, as `capcomd profiles validate`).

put.description: Capability profiles.edit. Change a profile: each field by id with its new value (or null to remove it), and the `rev` it was read with. Needs the `configure` scope (403 `forbidden` without it: a profile is what every later agent of it runs with) and an `Idempotency-Key` (the same key with the same request replays the first 200; with another, 409 `idempotency_conflict`). Written to the profile's own file (`writesTo`), atomically, keeping a YAML file's comments; a profile file's `version` goes up by one (an agents.json entry has none and stays 1). Agents already spawned keep the spec and version they started with; the next spawn uses the new one. Every write that changed something is audited: a durable profile.changed event on the `daemon` stream. Answers like GET /v1/profiles/{name}, with `changed` and `changes`. 409 `conflict` when `rev` isn't the current one (the body carries the current `rev`: read the profile again, then retry). 422 `invalid` with `field` for a field it doesn't have or that isn't `editable`, or a value not of its type; 422 `invalid` when the profiles the change would leave can't be read (a value out of range, a widening child, a missing parent: `message` says which, as `capcomd profiles validate`), which writes nothing. 404 `not_found` for a name that isn't a profile.

get.description:
SSE. Each event frame: `id: <seq>`, `event: <type>`, `data: <envelope JSON>`. Resume by sending `Last-Event-ID: <seq>`.
If that seq was compacted away, or this client's buffer overflowed (slow reader), the server sends `event: stream.reset` with {snapshotSeq, reason},
then `snapshot.*` frames ending with `snapshot.end`, then live events from snapshotSeq+1. Handle both reasons the same way: drop local state, apply the snapshot.
A `: heartbeat` comment every 15s; treat ~45s of silence as a dead socket. There is no global stream: subscribe to `daemon` and open a run stream on drill-in.
The SSE `event:` field is the frame type: the envelope's dotted `type` for events, else `stream.reset` or `snapshot.*`.
Run scopes accept `?feed=lifecycle`: no snapshot.steps/threads, only lifecycle events (below) after the snapshot, and `?activity=1`: live, ephemeral agent.activity_changed frames (at most one per agent per second), and `?thread=1`: live, ephemeral agent.thread_item_changed frames (Agent threads, below).
Timestamps (ts, decidedAt, expiresAt): RFC 3339 UTC with exactly 3 millisecond digits, e.g. 2026-10-25T07:57:00.000Z.

message.description: Agent-written text (here what went wrong, which may quote the plugin's error): render as plain text

effect.description: denied (the operation was refused, naming the plugin) or skipped (the listener was left out)

PluginHookFailedData.description: Capability plugins. Durable, on the `daemon` stream (and GET /v1/events?scope=daemon); `entity` is plugin:<name>; the envelope text is daemon-written. One call to a plugin's hook listener produced no usable answer (spec §6.5)

PluginSuspendedData.description: Capability plugins. Durable, on the `daemon` stream (and GET /v1/events?scope=daemon); `entity` is plugin:<name>; the envelope text is daemon-written. The breaker tripped: the plugin's listeners are no longer called (its gate listeners deny) until it is enabled again or the daemon restarts (spec §6.5)

PluginResumedData.description: Capability plugins. Durable, on the `daemon` stream (and GET /v1/events?scope=daemon); `entity` is plugin:<name>; the envelope text is daemon-written. A suspended plugin's listeners are called again

event.description: started, disconnected (its hooks stream has been closed for 60 s: its gate calls fail), reconnected, exited, restarting (more may come)

code.description: exited: its exit code; null when a signal ended it, and for the other events

restarts.description: Its exits in the last 10 minutes: at 5 it is failed with cause restart_limit

PluginProcessChangedData.description: Capability plugins.protocol. Durable, on the `daemon` stream (and GET /v1/events?scope=daemon); `entity` is plugin:<name>; the envelope text is daemon-written. An out-of-process plugin's process changed (spec §9.5): each start has a new session and token; a gate call in flight when it exited was denied

state.description: new, idle, running or unknown; failed or cancelled when the run ended without its agents ending it (a failed start, Stop on a run with no agent running: `run.ended`); starting in the runs.create response, before the run's process has registered it

Older daemons don't send it

profileSource.description: The layer its profile was found in at spawn: project (the project's .capcomd/profiles/ or .capcomd/agents.json), user (~/.capcomd/profiles/ or the user's agents.json) or bundled (shipped with capcomd). text.description: Plain-language status line written by the daemon (trusted)

text.description: Plain-language line, sentence case, no period, written by the daemon (trusted): progressive while the agent works ("Reading 4 files"), past tense once it stopped ("Read 4 files")

kind.description: Icon hint: read, edit, write, search, run, test, build, install, check, git, web, spawn, wait, message, verify, merge, report, delegate, plan, think, tool. More may be added: treat an unknown kind as tool

result.description: Agent-written text: the agent's declared result. Render every string as plain text, never markdown, links or actions

repo.description: Repository the agent works in: absolute path or remote URL, without credentials. Today always the run's repository

provider.description: The AI provider the agent runs on: claude or codex; null for a fake (local stand-in) agent

model.description: The model the agent runs with, when the daemon knows it (the profile's model or CAPCOMD_AGENT_MODEL); null: the provider CLI's default, or a fake agent

effort.description: The reasoning effort the agent runs with (its profile's, the run's chosen level for its planner, or CAPCOMD_AGENT_EFFORT): one of its provider's levels (GET /v1/run-options `efforts`); null: the provider CLI's default, or a fake agent

createdAt.description: When it was spawned (a client's elapsed clock starts here); null when unknown. Older daemons don't send it

updatedAt.description: RFC 3339 UTC with exactly 3 millisecond digits, e.g. 2026-10-25T07:57:00.000Z

title.description: Agent-written text: render as plain text, never markdown, links or actions

titleSource.description: Where Agent.title comes from: user (renamed in an app or with PUT …/title; it sticks until they clear it), self (the agent named itself: `capcomd title` in its VM), parent (its parent named it: `spawn --title`, `capcomd title <child>`), driver (the user's driving harness: capcomd_title, `capcomd title <runId> <agt>`), derived (nobody did: the daemon's, from the task's first words). More may be added: show the title whatever its source

approvalId.description: Stable approval id, carried on approval events; decide with it directly

question.description: Agent-written text: render as plain text, never markdown, links or actions

requestedBy.description: Who asked; ancestors of agentId may decide within their budget cap

target.description: merge: the branch it lands on

ref.description: merge: the branch (or ref) being merged

files.description: merge: the files the branch changes, `git diff --numstat` of the verified commit against where its branch left the target, the 20 with the most changed lines first (then by path). path.description: Agent-written text: render as plain text, never markdown, links or actions

removed.description: Lines removed; null for a binary file

added.description: merge: lines added across all its files (binary files not counted)

removed.description: merge: lines removed across all its files (binary files not counted)

askedBy.description: merge: the agent that asked for it and waits on the decision (requestedBy.agentId is the agent whose work merges). Absent for an operator's merge and on older daemons

heldBy.description: merge: a plugin held it for this approval (merge.landing): the plugin and its reason, which the question repeats. Approving satisfies only this hold: a merge another plugin then holds asks again. Absent when only the target's protection asks, and on older daemons

plugin.description: The plugin that held the merge

reason.description: Agent-written text (here the plugin's own words): render as plain text

holdId.description: The plugin's own name for this hold, when it gave one: approving satisfies a later hold of this plugin with the same holdId, whatever its reason says then; absent when the plugin named none (the reason identifies the hold). Plugin-written: render as plain text

subject.description: Kind-specific detail: merge {target, ref, files, filesTotal, added, removed}, budget {add}, egress {host}, secret {name}, spawn_widen {limits}

requestedAt.description: When it was asked (a merge: when it was parked); absent on daemons that predate it

seq.description: Resume cursor; persisted per scope with the event write, stable across daemon restarts

type.description: Dotted lowercase: the kernel's are noun.verb_past (run.created, merge.approval_requested); a plugin's own are plugin.<plugin name>.<event> (plugin.gate-reviewer.verdict), written only by that plugin. Show a type you don't know by its envelope text

ts.description: RFC 3339 UTC with exactly 3 millisecond digits, e.g. 2026-10-25T07:57:00.000Z

text.description: Plain-language sentence for this step, written by the daemon from trusted fields only. On a plugin's own event (plugin.<plugin name>.<event>) it is that plugin's sentence instead: render it as plain text, never markdown, links or actions

steps.description: Recent durable events of the scope, oldest first (step history)

at.description: RFC 3339 UTC with exactly 3 millisecond digits, e.g. 2026-10-25T07:57:00.000Z

text.description: Agent-written text: render as plain text, never markdown, links or actions

attachment.description: Full text stored by the daemon; fetch it with attachments.get

id.description: Stable: an update has the same id and a higher rev

seq.description: Run-wide cursor, advanced by every write (create or update): ?after=<seq> returns items created or changed since

order.description: Position in the thread: sort by this (it never changes)

kind.description: say, thinking, tool, error, result, plan, handoff, other. More may be added: render an unknown kind as a plain line of `text`

status.description: open: a tool call still running (or, later, a message still streaming); done: final

at.description: When it started (ISO 8601 UTC, ms precision)

durationMs.description: tool: as the CLI reported it (Glob, Grep, WebFetch, WebSearch, Task); null otherwise

text.description: Agent-written text: the item as plain text, for copy, search and kinds a client doesn't know: the message (cut at a block boundary like blocks), the tool summary, the error, or a one-line summary. Plain text: never markdown, HTML, or a link to follow

redacted.description: thinking: the CLI withheld the text (redacted or empty)

callId.description: The CLI's call id (Claude tool_use id, Codex item id)

name.description: Agent-written text: the tool's name as the CLI reported it (Read, Bash, command_execution, capcomd.capcomd_spawn). Plain text: never markdown, HTML, or a link to follow

kind.description: Icon hint, Agent.activity's kinds (read, edit, run, test, …); treat an unknown one as tool

summary.description: Agent-written text: one line built by the daemon from the call's fields, e.g. "Read ids/v1/schema.json", "Run bun test". Plain text: never markdown, HTML, or a link to follow

args.description: Agent-written text: the call's input as JSON, at most 4 KB. Plain text: never markdown, HTML, or a link to follow

output.description: Agent-written text: the result's text, at most 16 KB (the end kept); null while open. Plain text: never markdown, HTML, or a link to follow

files.description: Files the call wrote or changed, as file links

diff.description: A file-editing call's change (Claude Code Edit, MultiEdit, Write, NotebookEdit insert): from the call's input while it runs, replaced by the result's own patch (with context) when it returns. isError: the change was proposed but not applied

path.description: Agent-written text: the file, relative to the workspace root, '/'-separated, normalized like file links (never ..); null when it is outside the workspace. Plain text: never markdown, HTML, or a link to follow

added.description: Lines added by the whole change (not only the lines shown)

removed.description: Lines removed by the whole change (not only the lines shown)

op.description: " ": context, "+": added, "-": removed, "@": a gap between two hunks (lines in between not shown; `text` is the next hunk's `@@ -a,b +c,d @@` header when the CLI reported line numbers, else empty). Render an unknown op as context

text.description: Agent-written text: the line, without its newline, at most 240 characters (an ellipsis when cut); indentation kept. Plain text: never markdown, HTML, or a link to follow

lines.description: The change's first lines, at most 40 (separators included). Context lines are only lines the CLI's event contained: no file is read

truncatedLines.description: Context, added and removed lines not shown

message.description: Agent-written text: what failed. Plain text: never markdown, HTML, or a link to follow

code.description: The CLI's code when it gave one (error_max_turns, rate_limit, turn_failed)

truncated.description: Over the per-item cap: whole trailing blocks were dropped (never cut inside a code block or table)

child.description: handoff: the child agent that handed back (its summary is the blocks; artifacts are links and media)

lang.description: Agent-written text: the fence's info word. Plain text: never markdown, HTML, or a link to follow

text.description: Agent-written text: code, newlines kept. Plain text: never markdown, HTML, or a link to follow

alt.description: Agent-written text: alt text. Plain text: never markdown, HTML, or a link to follow

anyOf.description: Remote media never loads by itself; attachment, inline and workspace media load through the daemon only

text.description: Agent-written text: the trailing block still being written. Plain text: never markdown, HTML, or a link to follow

anyOf.description: Reserved for token streaming: the last block of an open say/thinking item, as plain text. Not emitted yet

target.description: Classified by the daemon. web: http(s) only; artifact: an attachment the daemon holds (id); file: a path in the agent's workspace (path); agent / run: a capcomd id (id); none: anything else (javascript:, data:, mailto:, custom schemes, paths outside the workspace): show `text` as plain text
